newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Sept 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Sept 24.

text.p: Ultramar Corp agreed to merge with Diamond Shamrock Inc in a deal that values Diamond Shamrock at $1 billion and Ultramar at $1.35 billion, the Wall Street Journal reported on Tuesday.
Meanwhile, the Chicago Board Options Exchange (CBOE) began investigating heavy trading last week of Diamond Shamrock call options.

* The Canadian Auto Workers chose General Motors Corp as its next target for contract talks. Separately, the United Auto Workers has not said whether it will focus its next set of talks on GM or Chrysler Corp.
* Prudential Insurance Co of America will pay at least $410 million to settle lawsuits that allege the company misled policyholders into buying more costly insurance.
* A Horizon/CMS Healthcare Corp nursing home in Michigan was raided last week by the Michigan Attorney General's office.
* Goldman Sachs & Co plans to create a new tier of junior partners.
* Big B Inc rejected a $330 million takeover offer from Revco D.S. Inc.
* Mossimo Inc's stock price fell 17 percent after the company said its costs would hurt profits.
* The Federal Trade Commission recommended tighter privacy protection of consumer data.
* Warner Bros, a unit of Time Warner Inc, will release a movie this fall that stars basketball superstar Michael Jordan and cartoon character Bugs Bunny.
* The Dow Jones industrial average rose to another record, while bond prices advanced despite fears of an interest-rate hike coming out of Tuesday's meeting of Federal Reserve Board policy makers.
* Apple Computer Inc named a new general manager for the unit that makes its PowerBook laptop computers.
* OptiMark Technologies Inc will unveil a new trading system that would permit institutional investors to place large orders while keeping the customer anonymous.
* The bears are getting their fur singed again in the stock market. To understand how, just look at Chesapeake Energy . - Heard on the Street
